- When sentiment is predominantly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 2–5% for 3–7 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or mixed, model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–4% for next 5–10 days.
- Model consistently underestimates in early part of 30-day horizon (days 1–7) — apply upward bias of 1–3% for first 7 days.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from 1.00 to 0.00) within 3–5 days, model lags; adjust forecast to reflect sentiment shift 1–2 days ahead.
- Mean reversion bias: if price is above 30-day moving average, reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 5 days; if below, increase by 1–2%.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven volatility — weight sentiment history more heavily in early days (days 1–5) for adjustment.
